items.title: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 ufficiale. Per chi vuole il massimo c'è la versione Extreme
items.summary: Qualcomm toglie i veli al suo nuovo processore top di gamma. Con una sorpresa: per i produttori che vorranno realizzare un prodotto "ultra" arriva anche una versione Extreme. Il nome? Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Stesso nome, due modelli: Qualcomm quest'anno proporrà ai partner due differenti versioni di processore top di gamma, lo Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 e lo Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Non ci troviamo davanti, come si potrebbe pensare, allo stesso processore con il modello "estremo" leggermente più spinto: sono due chip differenti anche nel packaging , con il modello Extreme che fa debuttare una soluzione sviluppata da Qualcomm, Offset Pop, grazie alla quale le memorie non sono più posizionate sopra il processore, come avviene storicamente con i SoC per smartphone, ma sono spostate leggermente di lato . Non di fianco, come sui nuovi A20 Pro, ma leggermente spostate per scoprire una parte di processore, che potrà quindi smaltire più facilmente il calore.

La mossa di Qualcomm non sorprende: la versione "extreme" dei processori aveva già debuttato lo scorso anno con l'X2 Elite, il top di gamma della famiglia compute, e ora si estende anche al mobile per dare più opzioni a chi produce smartphone.

Per chi se lo stesse chiedendo l'erede del top di gamma dello scorso anno è lo Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 : la versione Extreme è qualcosa in più.

Commercialmente la mossa è sensata: oggi l'unico produttore che può permettersi di far realizzare a Qualcomm una versione speciale del suo processore è Samsung, con lo Snapdragon for Galaxy; tutti gli altri non hanno i numeri. Sul mercato, però, soprattutto negli ultimi anni, sono spuntate le versioni "Ultra" dei flagship, e i vari produttori come Xiaomi, OPPO e vivo hanno dovuto usare lo stesso processore che usavano sulla versione "pro".

L'Extreme è la soluzione, anche se va detto che arriva in un momento di mercato delicato, in cui i produttori già faticano a gestire l'aumento di prezzo di RAM e storage e ora si trovano anche a dover scegliere se spendere per il processore quanto spendevano lo scorso anno oppure, per poter dare agli utenti il prodotto migliore possibile, spendere qualcosa di più e prendere l'Extreme. Con un ovvio aumento di prezzo del prodotto finale che potrebbe raggiungere, secondo alcuni analisti incontrati al Summit di Qualcomm, i 1999 euro per la versione da 16 GB di RAM.

Sia il Gen 6 sia l'Extreme sono realizzati da TSMC sullo stesso nodo a 2 nanometri usato da Apple per l'A20 Pro dei nuovi iPhone. Se pensiamo che i primi prodotti con processore Qualcomm arriveranno sul mercato a brevissimo, lo Xiaomi 18 Pro verrà annunciato oggi a Pechino, si può notare che Apple non ha avuto, come in passato con i 3 nm, un anno di esclusiva sul processo produttivo.

Guardando alla CPU, basata sui core Oryon di quarta generazione, entrambi i chip montano due core Prime che toccano per la prima volta la soglia dei 5,0 GHz, affiancati da sei core Performance fino a 4,0 GHz.

È la prima volta che un processore mobile raggiunge questa frequenza, circa l'8,5% in più rispetto alla frequenza di picco della generazione precedente.

Sulla CPU non c'è quindi alcuna differenza di clock tra i due modelli, anche se Qualcomm dichiara un incremento di prestazioni CPU rispetto alla generazione precedente del 10% per il Gen 6 e del 13% per l'Extreme, con un consumo della CPU inferiore del 37% su entrambi.

La motivazione è nella soluzione di packaging con il package superiore, quello con le memorie, sfalsato: grazie a questa soluzione l'Extreme riesce a sostenere meglio le prestazioni nel tempo, a parità di sistema di dissipazione, e quindi a tenere valori leggermente più elevati, che portano a un risultato migliore nei benchmark.

Rispetto allo scorso anno cambia anche l'architettura della cache, con l'introduzione del nuovo Oryon FlexCache . Lo Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 aveva 12 MB di cache L2 dedicati esclusivamente ai core Prime e altri 12 MB esclusivamente ai Performance, per 24 MB complessivi ma rigidamente separati per tipo di core. Il FlexCache introduce invece un pool condiviso da 16 MB accessibile da tutti gli otto core indipendentemente dalla loro natura: la cache nominale complessiva si riduce, ma un singolo core può ora attingere a una quantità di memoria condivisa più grande quando ne ha bisogno, riducendo gli sconfinamenti verso la DRAM, più lenta e meno efficiente. È la prima volta che Qualcomm introduce un pool condiviso tra tipologie di core diverse.

Le due piattaforme supportano sia memoria LPDDR5X-10600 sia la nuova LPDDR6-10600, oltre allo standard di storage UFS 5.0, che raddoppia la banda per lane rispetto a UFS 4.0 arrivando fino a 46,4 Gbit/s. La banda di memoria, con memorie LPDDR6-10600, dovrebbe arrivare a 113 GB/s, contro gli 84,8 GB/s del Gen 5 con LPDDR5X-5300.

Entrambi i chip montano una nuova generazione di NPU Hexagon riprogettata, con una configurazione dichiarata di 12 unità scalari, 8 vettoriali, una tensor e un'ulteriore unità di calcolo chiamata Element Accelerator. È un blocco di calcolo dedicato alle cosiddette operazioni elementwise: somme, moltiplicazioni, confronti e funzioni di attivazione applicate a singoli valori di un tensore, indipendentemente l'uno dall'altro. Affianca le unità scalari, che gestiscono valori singoli e compiti di controllo, e quelle vettoriali, che processano molti valori in parallelo, scaricandole da operazioni ripetitive che altrimenti impegnerebbero risorse di calcolo generiche.

A completare il quadro ci sono Hexagon Direct Link, il micro tile inferencing e la virtualizzazione della memoria a 64 bit, con supporto alle precisioni da INT2 a INT16 e ai formati FP8 e FP16.

Qualcomm continua a considerare, come Google, la NPU il processore migliore per gestire modelli generativi, ma aveva bisogno di ridurre i tempi di risposta e migliorare l'efficienza del reasoning multi-step degli agenti AI, quindi ha aggiunto un blocco specifico e lo ha fatto su entrambe le versioni.

Le prestazioni IA non sono però identiche: sul Gen 6 la NPU cresce del 14% in prestazioni e del 20% in prestazioni per watt, mentre sull'Extreme si arriva rispettivamente al 35% e al 33%.

Sulla versione Extreme è stata infatti aumentata la quantità di memoria dedicata alla NPU, Qualcomm dice che è maggiorata del 50%, ma non ne dichiara la dimensione esatta in megabyte, e questa memoria è pensata per tenere vicino ai core di calcolo lo stato corrente del modello, il contesto e la KV-cache, riducendo così gli accessi alla memoria di sistema.

Grazie a questa memoria l'Extreme può gestire modelli MoE (Mixture of Experts) oltre i 30 miliardi di parametri, con finestre di contesto fino a 32.000 token, senza la necessità di avere a bordo dello smartphone un quantitativo di memoria enorme. Abbiamo assistito a una demo, e la velocità che si riesce a raggiungere è di circa 30 token al secondo con un reference smartphone dotato però di 24 GB di RAM.

Se sull'Elite Gen 6 arriva una versione migliorata della GPU Adreno già usata lo scorso anno, sempre con tre slice di calcolo, sulla versione Extreme debuttano sia gli Adreno Matrix Core sia Adreno Neural Fusion, la tecnologia di rendering AI che sfrutta proprio i Matrix Core per offrire super resolution e frame generation in pieno stile DLSS 4.

Al lancio Adreno Neural Fusion sarà supportata da Unreal Engine, Unity e dal motore Messiah di NetEase, e i giochi realizzati con questi motori, se compilati con supporto all'SDK Snapdragon, potranno beneficiare di upscaling e frame generation , riducendo notevolmente l'impatto sul processore e con un risparmio notevole di batteria a parità di frame rate.

Qualcomm dichiara una riduzione della potenza di rendering fino al 40% e cita tra i titoli in arrivo Honkai: Star Rail, Monster Hunter Outlanders, Diablo Immortal, War Thunder Mobile, Arena Breakout e Farming Simulator 26.

L'azienda ci ha spiegato inoltre che nonostante i Matrix Core siano stati messi nella GPU per poter usare modelli generativi su elementi grafici tenendo la latenza bassissima, è anche possibile utilizzarli per l'IA generativa , seppur con un consumo più elevato rispetto a quello della NPU.

Su entrambe le varianti troviamo 18 MB di memoria dedicata Adreno HPM (High Performance Memory) con un'architettura migliorata che promette il 12% di risparmio energetico rispetto alla generazione precedente, e un clock che sale a 1,45 GHz, 225 MHz in più rispetto all'Adreno 840 del Gen 5. Qualcomm dichiara un incremento di prestazioni GPU del 35% per il Gen 6 e del 44% per l'Extreme, con efficienza migliorata fino al 40%.

Sul fronte fotografico entrambi i chip condividono lo stesso triplo ISP Qualcomm Spectra a 20 bit, con supporto nativo agli ultimi sensori HDR lanciati da produttori come OmniVision, Samsung e Sony: tecnologie come LOFIC, DCG, DCG+VS e Staggered HDR possono quindi essere gestite direttamente dalla pipeline d'immagine, senza dover ricorrere a elaborazioni software per ricostruire il segnale HDR. Arriva anche l'Intelligent Pixel Control, che analizza la scena pixel per pixel, e il supporto fino a 320 MP di risoluzione.

Sul video, però, la variante più potente è l'unica a offrire registrazione fino a 8K a 60 fps e slow motion fino a 4K a 240 fps, questo grazie a un ISP con throughput dati fino a 4 volte superiore.

items.title: Transit rewards
items.summary: Article URL: https://waymo.com/blog/2026/09/transit-rewards/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49811065 Points: 185 # Comments: 230
items.content:
Today, Waymo is excited to announce our transit rewards program, which we will initially offer in the San Francisco Bay Area, with future cities to follow. This first-of-its-kind initiative rewards riders with Waymo Cash when they connect their Waymo rides with public transit and use their Visa card. We’ll start with employee access before gradually rolling out to the public in the coming weeks.

Public transit networks and shared autonomous vehicles are part of a complementary mobility ecosystem. As transit agencies modernize their payment systems to accept tap-to-pay debit and credit cards, multimodal trips are becoming more convenient than ever.

"Governor Newsom has challenged all of us to build a transportation system that meets Californians where they are, and that means making the trip to the station as effortless as the train ride itself," said California Transportation Secretary Toks Omishakin. "CalSTA welcomes innovations that reward people for choosing transit and make a multimodal trip feel like one seamless journey."

Recent surveys show that over 50% of Waymo riders in our most mature service areas (San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix) use public transit, so we’re proud to invest directly in this connectivity to make everyday commutes easier and more affordable. The transit rewards program works alongside the regional transfer discount programs and tap-to-pay model launched in the San Francisco Bay Area last December. The program applies to all 27 San Francisco Bay Area transit agencies that accept contactless Visa tap-to-pay.

“San José has always believed innovation should make everyday life work better,” said San José Mayor Matt Mahan. “This partnership does exactly that by using new technology to strengthen public transit, not replace it, making regional travel more seamless and giving people more ways to get where they need to go.”

To participate, riders will link their Visa card in the Waymo app. When riders in the SF Bay Area use their Visa card to take a Waymo trip and public transit within 2 hours of each other, we will automatically issue $2.85 in Waymo Cash, which is the cost of a bus fare in San Francisco.

Alongside the launch of our transit rewards program, we’re also announcing a partnership with Caltrain, which accepts tap-to-pay. Waymo will lease 40 dedicated Caltrain station parking spaces to better serve transit riders with staged vehicles. This is a model we hope to replicate with additional transit agencies, ultimately enabling more seamless connections between Waymo’s service and public transit.

This launch is the next step toward making our vision of shared mobility a reality. By taking the learnings from our transit credit pilot programs in San Francisco and Los Angeles , adding Waymo’s service to the LA Metro Mobility Wallet program, and kicking off a strategic microtransit partnership with Via in Chandler, AZ, we’ve been steadily learning what it takes to offer a successful transit integration product and are pleased to formally launch transit rewards.

“Shared mobility is a team effort, and our autonomous ride-hailing service helps expand clean transportation options for everyone,” said Adam Lenz, Head of Sustainability & Environment at Waymo. “We’re thrilled to partner with local transit agencies to fill multimodal gaps and make daily commutes easier through our new transit rewards program.”

Our goal is to expand this transit rewards program and transit agency partnerships to more cities over time, ultimately making shared, all-electric transportation more accessible and affordable for everyone.

items.title: Captato un segnale radio da un esopianeta
items.summary: Captato un segnale radio da un esopianeta
items.content:
Non ci sono ancora prove dell'esistenza di vita oltre la Terra, ma gli astronomi continuano a scandagliare il cielo alla ricerca di segnali che indichino che non siamo soli nell'Universo. E ora un gruppo del Center for Astrophysics Harvard & Smithsonian e dell'Università dell'Oregon ha messo a segno un primato storico: la prima rilevazione diretta di onde radio provenienti da un esopianeta, cioè un pianeta esterno al Sistema Solare.
Finora, ogni segnale radio individuato nei sistemi planetari extrasolari non poteva essere attribuito con certezza al pianeta stesso, ma solo, più genericamente, alla stella attorno a cui orbita. Questa volta, però, i ricercatori sono riusciti a isolare l'origine esatta dell'emissione.. Aurore non alieni
Niente alieni in cerca di contatto, va detto subito: il segnale nasce dalle aurore del pianeta, prodotte dall'interazione tra particelle cariche, atmosfera e campo magnetico, un fenomeno che rilascia energia sotto forma di onde radio. Anche la Terra ha le sue aurore, boreali e australi, generate dallo stesso tipo di meccanismo.
«Sebbene le esplosioni radio aurorali siano già state osservate nei pianeti del Sistema Solare e in alcune nane ultrafredde, finora nessuna rilevazione radio era stata attribuita in modo inequivocabile a un pianeta extrasolare piuttosto che alla sua stella ospite», scrivono i ricercatori nel loro articolo pubblicato su arXiv.. Beta Pictoris b, il gigante gassoso sotto osservazione
Le frequenze sono state monitorate con il radiotelescopio MeerKAT, in Sudafrica, in quattro sessioni di osservazione condotte tra il 2025 e il 2026. Bersaglio delle osservazioni: la stella Beta Pictoris, distante circa 63,4 anni luce dalla Terra, attorno alla quale orbitano tre pianeti noti - Beta Pictoris b, c e d. . Dalle osservazioni sono emersi brevi impulsi radio ripetuti, caratterizzati da una forte polarizzazione circolare: una firma tipica delle emissioni aurorali. Usando come riferimento nella mappa celeste i quasar, nuclei galattici estremamente luminosi, gli scienziati sono riusciti a stabilire con un alto grado di certezza che a emettere il segnale fosse il pianeta b e non la stella. Un dettaglio non scontato, perché Beta Pictoris è una stella giovane - più calda, più grande e strutturalmente diversa dal nostro Sole - e «nessun meccanismo fisico noto per l'emissione radio nelle stelle di questo tipo può spiegare quanto osservato», precisano gli autori dello studio.. Un indizio sul campo magnetico del pianeta
Le caratteristiche del segnale rimandano a un fenomeno chiamato "instabilità maser a ciclotrone elettronico" (ECMI), lo stesso meccanismo che genera le aurore su Terra e Giove. E gli ECMI non sono solo la firma di un'aurora: forniscono anche informazioni preziose sull'intensità del campo magnetico del pianeta che le produce.
Secondo i calcoli del team, Beta Pictoris b possiede un campo magnetico particolarmente intenso - migliaia di volte più forte di quello terrestre - un dato coerente con i modelli teorici elaborati in precedenza sulla "dinamo" del pianeta, cioè i processi interni che generano il magnetismo planetario.
«Questa rappresenta la prima misurazione diretta dell'intensità del campo magnetico di un esopianeta, ed è coerente con le previsioni basate sulla dinamo per un giovane pianeta gigante massiccio», scrivono i ricercatori. L'emissione aurorale sarebbe alimentata dalla rotazione estremamente rapida del pianeta, che compie un giro completo su se stesso in appena 8-9 ore.. Un gigante da record
Beta Pictoris b è stato scoperto nel 2008 e ha una massa pari a circa 10 volte quella di Giove, tanto da avvicinarsi per dimensioni alle nane brune, oggetti celesti a metà strada tra un pianeta molto massiccio e una stella mancata. Proprio per questo un campo magnetico così potente non sorprende gli scienziati: fenomeni simili erano già stati osservati sulle nane brune. Ora il pianeta si aggiudica anche il primato di essere il primo esopianeta da cui sia mai stato rilevato un segnale radio inequivocabile.. Non tutti gli esperti, va detto, considerano la questione definitivamente chiusa: secondo alcuni astronomi che hanno commentato lo studio, la prova più convincente arriverà quando si osserverà il segnale pulsare con la stessa periodicità della rotazione del pianeta, dato che l'aurora dovrebbe entrare e uscire dal campo visivo man mano che il pianeta ruota.. Prossimi obiettivi
Forti di questo risultato, i ricercatori hanno già puntato lo sguardo su altri sette esopianeti giganti noti, distribuiti in cinque sistemi stellari vicini, che potrebbero presto essere analizzati con lo stesso metodo usato per Beta Pictoris b.
«Un miglioramento della sensibilità degli strumenti di circa 5-7 volte, previsto per gli osservatori radio di nuova generazione, li renderà rilevabili», concludono gli autori dello studio..

items.title: Playing loud music on the bus? That will cost you hundreds of dollars in Singapore
items.summary: Authorities are cracking down on "disruptive behaviours" including eating onboard and putting feet on seats.
items.content:
Bus passengers in Singapore can now be fined up to $500 Singapore dollars ($391; £293) for placing their feet on seats or playing loud audio, as well as eating, drinking or littering onboard.

A fine of up to $5,000 will be imposed for more serious offences, such as causing obstruction or danger to fellow commuters within bus terminals or "the soiling of any part of a public bus, bus interchange, or terminal".

"These will foster a safer, more considerate and pleasant public transport environment for all," the Land Transport Authority (LTA) said in a news release.

The new regulations, announced on Monday, align with existing rules on Singapore's railway, or Mass Rapid Transit (MRT), network.

But while there have long been punishments for MRT passengers caught eating onboard, for example, rules on buses were typically company policies enforced by drivers, who could ask commuters to alight.

Now these nuisance behaviours have become official legal offences carrying immediate fines.

Authorised bus staff – such as ticket inspectors and bus interchange staff – can issue official notices to passengers who are suspected of committing an offence, according to LTA.

Bus drivers - or "captains", as they are called in Singapore - will not be given the same authority, leaving them to prioritise their duty of safely operating the bus. They can, however, tell commuters to stop disruptive behaviour, and those who refuse to cooperate may be asked to alight the bus or, in severe cases, face police intervention.

Singapore is not alone in trying to make public transport more peaceful. As transit networks grow, cities around the world are actively cracking down on bad behaviour to ensure a peaceful commute for all passengers.

Earlier this year, the Polish city of Kraków introduced similar rules with commuters now facing a fine of up to 200 złoty ($52; £39) for "disturbing the peace and quiet within the vehicle" with their mobile phones and other electronic devices.

In the United Kingdom, existing laws ban "anti-social behaviour" on trains and stations, including using "sound-producing equipment" without permission if it annoys others.

Some politicians have pushed to specifically fine so-called "headphone dodgers" - people who play loud music and videos - across all public transport, including buses, with fines of up to £1,000.

These rules in Singapore, Kraków, and the United Kingdom show a growing trend of transport authorities stepping in to protect passengers.

"Public transport is a shared space, and every commuter has a part to play in ensuring a gracious and pleasant commuting environment," said Singapore's LTA.

items.title: US judge blocks deportation of DoorDash driver shot by ICE
items.summary: The delivery driver was transferred from a hospital to a detention centre after the shooting on Sunday.
items.content:
A US judge has temporarily blocked the deportation of a Venezuelan man who was shot by immigration agents in Texas, his lawyer says.

Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, is being held in a detention centre with a bullet in his back, according to his lawyer. Judge Orlando Garcia, a Clinton appointee, scheduled a hearing for Garces Perez to appear in court in person next week.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said in a statement that an "illegal alien" had been the subject of a targeted vehicle stop but pushed back against suggestions he had been given inadequate medical care.

The incident comes months after a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man in Houston.

Texas ICE shooting leaves Venezuelan DoorDash driver with bullet in his back, says lawyer

Garces Perez's immigration lawyer, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, has filed a federal lawsuit for a temporary restraining order to prevent his removal from the country.

Since the judge ordered that her client appear in person on 30 September, he cannot be deported before then, she said.

"For now, we have secured a temporary block on his deportation while his case moves forward," Lincoln-Goldfinch wrote on social media.

"This is an important step, but our work is not over," she wrote. "Wilber still needs appropriate medical care, and we will continue fighting to protect his rights."

The gunshot fractured his clavicle and he is wearing a sling while having "significant swelling and pain," Lincoln-Goldfinch said.

The cause or extent of the loss of movement he experienced has not yet been determined, she said.

A spokesperson for US Attorney's Office in Texas declined to comment on the case.

On Tuesday, DHS pushed back against what it called "false narratives" surrounding what had happened, blaming sanctuary cities and media for "spreading lies" and discouraging people from resisting officers and evading arrest.

"Contrary to their claims, this person is an illegal alien who has no legal status to be here and has been given some of the best medical care he's ever received in his life," said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin in a statement to the BBC.

DHS said the man, whom they did not name, was "the subject of a targeted vehicle stop" and that his work permit expired last year.

"No amount of smears and false narratives will slow down ICE from doing its job by removing dangerous illegal aliens from our communities and making America safe again," Mullin said.

The Austin Police Department, which was not involved in the incident, released dashcam and body camera footage on Tuesday showing its officers at the scene.

It does not show the shooting, but several gunshots can be heard in one dashcam clip, while another shows officers approaching Garces Perez's car and detaining him. At one point, Garces Perez's t-shirt is cut to reveal what appears to be a single gunshot in his back.

Lincoln-Goldfinch previously told the BBC that after being unable to move his arm in the detention facility, Garces Perez was taken back to hospital on Monday evening. He was treated there and has since been returned to the detention facility.

He said he was handcuffed, shackled at the ankles, placed in a waist chain, and handled roughly during his transfer, despite his injury, she said.

Lincoln-Goldfinch added that detention personnel had revoked his communication privileges and moved him from an infirmary into an isolated room with a flat, non-adjustable bed.

In its statement on Tuesday, DHS said Garces Perez had received medical care "around the clock" and denied claims he received no pain medication and was forced to sleep on the floor.

"This alien was released from the hospital and arrived at the detention facility just a few hours later, where he slept on a bed," DHS said.

Texas lawmaker Joaquin Castro, a Democrat, on Tuesday demanded the Venezuelan national's release from detention.

Local and state officials have pushed for an independent investigation into the shooting, which occurred just before on Sunday afternoon.

Hours later, dozens of protesters, some waving the flags of Mexico and Guatemala, gathered at the scene carrying signs demanding that ICE leave the city.

DHS said on Tuesday that ICE "will not be slowing down nor leaving Austin".

The man's lawyer told US media he was making a DoorDash delivery when an unmarked black truck sideswiped his car.

He did not know the truck was an ICE vehicle and made a U-turn, she said. His car was hit again before agents got out and shot him, according to the attorney.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, le news. Varsavia, elicottero russo viola lo spazio aereo polacco, caccia in volo
items.summary: Raid russo su Kiev, sospeso il servizio ferroviario della città. Il Cremlino dopo incontro Trump-Zelensky: “Non ci sono presupposti per colloqui di pace”. Lavrov arriva a New York, il primo impegno sarà il colloquio con Rubio
items.content:
Raid russi alle prime luci dell’alba su Kiev, colpiti magazzini e distributori di benzina di diversi quartieri della città: due morti e venititre feriti nella capitale, dove è stato sospeso il servizio ferroviario per via degli attacchi di Mosca.

Oggi, a margine dell'Assemblea generale delle Nazioni Unite a New York, si terrà un incontro fra il segretario di Stato americano Marco Rubio e il ministro degli Esteri russo Sergej Lavrov . L’appuntamento segue il colloquio fra Volodymyr Zelensky e Donald Trump dedicato al possibile rilancio dei negoziati per una via di uscita dalla guerra e a “un pacchetto invernale di forniture militari”.

Putin: “Alle elezioni tentativi di far deragliare il voto, ma che è impossibile spaventare la Russia”

Varsavia, elicottero russo viola lo spazio aereo, in volo i caccia

Lavrov arriva a New York, il primo impegno sarà il colloquio con Rubio

Raid russo su Kiev, sospeso il servizio ferroviario della città

“La nostra valutazione è che la minaccia russa ai Paesi Nato sia reale e di lunga durata". Lo ha dichiarato il segretario generale della Nato, Mark Rutte, intervenuto negli Stati uniti a un evento del Chicago Council on Global Affairs. "Nelle ultime due settimane abbiamo assistito ad attacchi ibridi, e a volte abbiamo avvistato droni. Abbiamo visto cosa è successo a Lipsia, e il governo tedesco ha chiaramente valutato che dietro c'è la Russia".

Zelensky: “Non è momento di cedere, all’Onu mantenere pressione su Russia”

"In ogni riunione dell'Assemblea Generale delle Nazioni Unite ci impegniamo a garantire un sostegno continuo all'Ucraina. Altrettanto importante è la giusta pressione esercitata sulla Russia attraverso le sanzioni". Lo ha scritto su 'X' il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky, che oggi interverrà all'Assemblea generale delle Nazioni Unite a New York. "L'Ucraina è grata a tutti coloro che agiscono e applicano una pressione basata sui principi. Praticamente tutti i nostri partner concordano sul fatto che, finché gli attacchi continuano, finché questa guerra terroristica prosegue, non è il momento di cedere", ha aggiunto Zelensky. "E' importante che le sanzioni inviino un segnale alla Russia, compresi i suoi oligarchi, che la guerra deve finire, non semplicemente aspettare che passi. Grazie a tutti coloro che stanno aiutando l'Ucraina", ha concluso Zelensky.

Putin: “Alle elezioni tentativi di far deragliare il voto, ma che è impossibile spaventare la Russia”

Il presidente russo Vladimir Putin, commentando le elezioni parlamentari, ha affermato che ci sono stati “tentativi di far deragliare il voto, ma che è impossibile spaventare la Russia”. Putin ha inoltre sottolineato l’affluenza record alle urne, sostenendo che il dato dimostra il sostegno della popolazione russa agli sforzi del governo “volti a rafforzare il Paese”. Putin si è rivolto anche ai militari russi, sottolineando il loro ruolo nel voto: “Queste elezioni sono anche per voi. Sono certo che tutti gli obiettivi dell’operazione militare speciale saranno raggiunti”.

Rutte: “Sicurezza dell’Ucraina è strettamente legata alla nostra”

"Che non ci siano dubbi: la sicurezza dell'Ucraina è strettamente legata alla nostra". Lo dichiara il segretario generale della Nato Mark Rutte nel corso della sua visita nello Stato dell'Iowa, intervenendo durante un evento ospitato dal Chicago Council on Global Affairs. L'Alleanza contribuisce a "garantire che l'Ucraina possa difendersi dall'aggressione in corso della Russia, con gli Stati Uniti che forniscono difese aeree chiave e altre attrezzature pagate dai vostri alleati Nato in Europa e Canada", afferma. Nel suo intervento Rutte sottolinea l'importanza degli "amici e alleati dell'America nella Nato" nel mantenimento della sicurezza in Europa, nell'Atlantico e nell'Artico, cosa che "contribuisce a mantenere sicura la patria degli Stati Uniti". Gli alleati degli Usa "forniscono anche basi e logistica cruciali, consentendo agli Stati Uniti di proiettare potenza lontano da casa: insieme, aiutiamo a mantenere la pace in Kosovo, uno stato partner dell'Iowa, e un luogo dove so che i membri della Guardia Nazionale dell'Iowa hanno fornito supporto e addestramento cruciale alle Forze di sicurezza del Kosovo tramite Kfor", aggiunge.

Varsavia, elicottero russo viola lo spazio aereo, in volo i caccia

La Polonia ha annunciato che questa mattina, a nord della località di Braniewo, si è verificata una breve violazione dello spazio aereo nazionale da parte di un elicottero Mi-8 delle Forze Armate della Federazione russa. "L'elicottero stava eseguendo un volo dalla regione di Kaliningrad. Ha violato lo spazio aereo polacco con una profondità massima di circa 300 m e vi ha sostato per 42 secondi", si legge nel comunicato del ministero della Difesa di Varsavia. Il volo dell'aeromobile è stato osservato dai sistemi radar delle Forze armate polacche e sono stati allertati aerei da caccia, mentre le Forze e i mezzi terrestri sono rimasti in stato di allerta. "La natura dell'incidente indica che la Russia sta testando nuovamente la prontezza della nostra difesa aerea", ha denunciato il ministero della Difesa, "gli equipaggi dei sistemi di difesa aerea della Polonia conducono un'osservazione continua 24 ore su 24, mantenendosi in costante prontezza per garantire la sicurezza dello spazio aereo polacco".

Ue a Kiev: “Procedere con le riforme, valgono 20 miliardi per il 2026”

La "lotta alla corruzione" e le misure sullo "stato di diritto" sono tra le riforme chiave chieste dall'Ue all'Ucraina per continuare con il programma di aiuto finanziario e "se tali riforme potessero essere attuate e adottate nel 2026 potrebbero sbloccare 20 miliardi di euro di sostegno al bilancio ". Lo ha detto un portavoce della Commissione Europea. "Il nostro messaggio, quindi, è che queste riforme sono state effettivamente concordate con le autorità ucraine e ratificate dalla Rada ed è quindi davvero importante che ora si proceda con la sua attuazione".

Attualmente non esistono i presupposti per avviare negoziati di pace sull'Ucraina, sebbene la Russia rimanga aperta a questa possibilità. Lo ha dichiarato il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitri Peskov . "La militarizzazione dell'Ucraina sta effettivamente proseguendo. Gli Stati europei cercano di reperire sempre più fondi per l'acquisto di armamenti. Il regime di Kiev continua la sua attività di stampo terroristico", ha detto Peskov ai giornalisti, commentando l'appello del presidente statunitense, Donald Trump, e del presidente ucraino, Volodymyr Zelensky , a favore di una tregua energetica. "Al momento non vi sono i presupposti per avviare negoziati di pace. Sebbene noi, come parte russa, restiamo aperti ai colloqui". Alla domanda se il Cremlino consideri pura retorica le dichiarazioni sulla necessità di una tregua, rilasciate sullo sfondo del sostegno militare attivo a Kiev, Peskov ha risposto: "Indubbiamente".

Cbs: “L’Ucraina pronta a firmare storico accordo con gli Usa in materia di droni”

L'Ucraina è pronta a firmare uno storico accordo di difesa con gli Stati Uniti in materia di droni, secondo tre fonti a conoscenza della questione. Lo scrive Cbs . Il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky è pronto a firmare l'accordo a margine dell'Assemblea generale delle Nazioni Unite questa settimana a New York, ma secondo alcune fonti l'accordo potrebbe essere finalizzato in un secondo momento, quando gli Stati Uniti saranno pronti a firmare. Nel corso dell'ultimo anno, il Dipartimento della Difesa e la sua controparte ucraina hanno sviluppato un quadro di riferimento che consentirebbe alle forze armate dei due Paesi di ampliare i test e la produzione di tecnologia di difesa ucraina negli Stati Uniti.

Un uomo è morto a causa di un attacco russo su Kiev e altre sette persone sono rimaste ferite. Lo ha riferito l'amministrazione militare della capitale ucraina su Telegram , secondo quanto riportato da Ukrinform. "Alle 10 del mattino, una persona è rimasta uccisa e sette ferite in un attacco ostile alla capitale ", si legge nel rapporto.

Lavrov arriva a New York, il primo impegno sarà il colloquio con Rubio

Il ministro degli Esteri Serghei Lavrov, che guida la delegazione russa all'Assemblea Generale dell'Onu, è arrivato a New York, dove il suo primo impegno sarà oggi un incontro con il segretario di Stato americano Marco Rubio . Lo ha detto la portavoce della diplomazia russa, Maria Zakharova. "Il nostro primo giro di incontri è in programma di primo mattino ora di New York, e comincerà con un colloquio con il segretario di Stato Rubio", ha sottolineato Zakharova in dichiarazioni a Radio Sputnik, riprese dalla Tass.

Raid russo su Kiev, sospeso il servizio ferroviario della città

Il servizio ferroviario urbano di Kiev è stato sospeso a causa di un attacco di droni sulla capitale avvenuto all'alba. Si sono registrati attacchi e incendi in diversi quartieri. Lo afferma il sindaco di Kiev Vitali Klitschko, come riportano i media locali. Secondo le prime ricostruzioni, i detriti provenienti da droni precipitati sarebbero caduti tra edifici residenziali e sui locali di una compagnia di trasporti nel distretto di Solomianskyi, dove è scoppiato un incendio. Droni hanno colpito e distrutto anche due distributori di benzina in diverse zone di Kiev. Nei raid su varie regioni ucraine sono stati utilizzati 161 droni.

items.title: Huge data centres rise at 'China speed' to power its AI ambitions
items.summary: The BBC visits Inner Mongolia, an unlikely frontier in Beijing's AI race with Washington.
items.content:
In the expansive grasslands of Inner Mongolia, farmers are picking plump potatoes alongside new neighbours: huge, rectangular blocks that will fuel China's AI platforms.

Ulanqab, with its steppes and volcanoes, is an unlikely digital frontier. For years, it has been China's official "potato capital". But now its fields have also become construction sites for a slew of data centres, as Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping meet to discuss AI safety among other things.

Hundreds of workers in yellow helmets carry heavy equipment into the building site as welding sparks fly off metal scaffolding. Above them huge cranes move with precision to build rooftops, while men balance on ladders to plaster brickwork.

"This is China speed," jokes one worker. "An infrastructure maniac," is how he describes his country, laughing as he walks away. “There is one phase every year. This is the second phase," explains an electrical engineer. "There will be many more phases afterwards."

Artifical intelligence sits at the heart of China's contest with the United States and the key to it is the computing power inside the data centres here.

To the Chinese Communist Party, these buildings are critical for the country's economic and national security. Once finished, they will help drive its mission to embed AI across 90% of industries and society by 2030.

China's not just building the infrastructure. It's also creating a pool of talent: young engineers and researchers who now see their country as a place of opportunity, partly because tensions with the US and Trump's restrictions on immigration have soured the American dream.

"Fewer students and researchers are heading to the US, and more are returning from the US to China. That is very clear," says Jack Zhang from the University of Science and Technology of China.

He himself was recruited by a high-level programme after studying at Yale in the US, and Cambridge in the UK.

"I wanted to take some of the AI work I was doing in the lab and apply it to human health and medicine. That requires more resources, more people and sometimes more government support, which can be difficult to access overseas."

China's expanding AI capabilities are one reason why the US says it doesn't want to hit pause on its AI development, despite stark warnings from inside the industry that the technology was moving too fast.

"Whoever wins AI, wins," President Trump said last week. The CEO of AI firm Anthropic, Dario Amodei, called for keeping the US-led ban on selling advanced chips and equipment to China, while warning that a Chinese lead would "pose grave danger for the US and the world".

This is not what Xi will want to hear when he arrives in Washington on Wednesday. The state-run Global Times, which echoes Beijing, dismissed US fears as part of a "Cold War playbook" to "contain" China's rise.

It is also touting an alternate model. Xi himself is encouraging Chinese AI firms to develop more affordable, open-source models - which allow people, companies and countries to modify it as they wish.

It also pits Chinese models against those in the US where developers including OpenAI and Anthropic use closed-model approaches, and their design elements are kept a secret.

One reason Beijing is in favour of their approach is that it has worked well for them. By sharing the tech, Chinese AI firms have been able to innovate quickly.

This has helped China overcome one of its biggest challenges: a lack of access to advanced chips, which would help unlock greater computing power.

But Beijing also wants a bigger say in writing the rules that govern AI. Xi has repeatedly called for more regulation and a global framework for others to follow.

With calls for AI safety growing, this week's summit at the White House is especially significant. Can the two sides collaborate on regulating AI? Is any talk of a slowdown even realistic?

It certainly doesn't seem like that in places like Ulanqab, where China's AI ambitions are taking shape.

China is building hundreds of data centres - for Huawei, ByteDance, DeepSeek - in sparsely-populated provinces: Ulanqab, Ningxia and Gansu in the north, Guizhou in the south-west.

It has already built up vast renewable energy capacity - wind and solar - in these regions, land is cheaper and the weather cooler, so there is less demand for water.

This doesn't mean there are no concerns or downsides. China wants most of its data centres to be fuelled by green energy by 2030 - but some of its grid is still fed by coal power. Water supply remains a concern in the arid, dry parts of Inner Mongolia.

Entire villages have been relocated, although it's hard to pin down the number or what compensation residents were offered. It's a topic few people will discuss because it can be dangerous to voice concerns too openly.

"This big data has absolutely nothing to do with ordinary people," says one local, speaking anonymously off camera. "What benefits has it brought us?"

He says few locals had found jobs there. Others told us of fears that their land would be taken and they would no longer be able to farm for a living.

But there are optimists too, such as a man who told us his last name was Zhang, standing alongside potato pickers in a field near the data centres.

“China is now at the forefront of the world," he says, adding that his children have managed to find jobs there.

"It's not like the 1960s, when it was relatively backward. China is doing alright now. Whether in economic development or other areas, it is doing well."

Surveys appear to suggest that there is little opposition to AI or its widespread adoption, compared to so many other countries, but it's hard to evaluate these figures in such a heavily-censored climate.

Beijing has been quite clear that it sees AI as a solution to its ageing workforce, and is rapidly automating manufacturing and production. That is producing anxiety over job losses, which, again, is hard to measure.

But this is also a country that is producing around five million science and tech graduates each year, compared to around half a million in the US.

And as more of them stay in China, they see a growing ecosystem for innovation.

AI developer Dang Ronghao, 27, who works for a leading tech company says Chinese campuses are becoming more open, allowing him to talk to researchers all over the world from his base in Shanghai.

"I've seen research combining AI with nuclear fusion, AI with astrophysics, AI with new materials, and AI with the development of new drugs. I think we are entering a good era."

Even so, some argue that China still rewards conformity over challenge. "It's not as open as I wish," says Professor Liu Jun, Department of Statistics and Data Science at Tsinghua University. He has taught at both Harvard and Stanford.

"I keep encouraging students here to ask more questions, to challenge more, but that's hard to change. I think partly it's culture, partly it's the system."

Far from the labs where Prof Liu and others are wrangling with the AI frontier, many Chinese people are still grappling with more immediate economic troubles: a sluggish economy, rising youth unemployment, low spending and property prices that have plummeted. In rural areas, an ageing population is also a growing concern.

"Big data and all that… pretty good – but it has nothing to do with me," says one farmer in Inner Mongolia, as he trundles on a cart to check on his sheep.

He says he has no use for AI. He hardly even uses the internet.

The screen on his phone is smashed, and wifi comes from a pocket dongle for which he pays just over 40 yuan a month.

"There haven't really been any changes for me. I don't know about the future," he says.

So much is changing here and everywhere else in the country, but it's hard to know how many people are as invested as their leaders in this tech-charged future.

Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding

China criticises idea it is in 'malicious competition' over AI

China is winning one AI race, the US another - but either might pull ahead

items.title: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
items.summary: The defence deal signed at the UN General Assembly also re-affirms Denmark's sovereignty over its semi-autonomous Arctic territory.
items.content:
The US, Denmark and Greenland have signed a defence deal that allows Washington to build two new military bases in the Arctic territory, while reaffirming Copenhagen's sovereignty over it.

Before a signing ceremony at the UN General Assembly in New York, US President Donald Trump said "we will immediately begin the process of developing a large military presence in the appropriate locations".

Danish PM Mette Frederiksen said the deal was "good for the US, Denmark and Greenland" and also for Europe and Nato, while Greenland's PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen said it was a "win-win-win".

The three leaders then inked the deal, seemingly ending more than a year of tension over the Arctic territory.

Trump had threatened to "take" the semi-autonomous Arctic territory over what he said were national security concerns, citing its strategic defence location and its mineral wealth.

His rhetoric prompted outcry from Greenlanders, Danes and European leaders who issued a joint statement saying his words "undermine transatlantic relations and risk a dangerous downward spiral".

The deal amends and updates a 1951 defence agreement between Denmark and the US.

The new pact says the US "shall be allowed to establish an additional Defence Area at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig" - referring to locations in Greenland's south and east.

Narsarsuaq is a former civilian airport and World War Two base. It has deep-water access and a large runway which US military engineers were recently surveying, the US North Command confirmed to the BBC.

The Mestersvig outpost is remote, far less developed, and used by a Danish naval dog sled unit.

The "modalities and technical details" of the bases are yet to be confirmed, and according to the deal, must be mutually agreed by all parties,

This means the US security arrangements are not unfettered and Greenland and Denmark's approval is still needed.

Washington currently operates its Pituffik Space Base in Greenland's north-west, and the new deal allows the US to "modernise and expand its activities" there.

It also says that "no state that is not a member of Nato shall be allowed to establish its own manned or unmanned military installations in Greenland nor shall they be allowed a persistent presence of military forces in Greenland".

Although the militaries of non-Nato countries are now explicitly barred from the island, it was highly unlikely that non-allied troops would have been allowed access in the first place.

Critically, no territory is ceded to the US, and it recognises both Denmark's "sovereignty and territorial integrity" and Greenland's right to self-determination.

On one hand, that's a significant climb down from Trump's earlier calls to acquire the Arctic island.

But it does deliver a strengthened US military presence and expand on the previous agreement. Therefore to some American eyes, that will be perceived as a historic win.

The new deal must still be approved by both Denmark's and Greenland's parliaments.

Despite months of crisis, the mood at Tuesday's signing ceremony appeared strikingly upbeat and friendly.

"We going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship," Trump said.

"This is tremendous for Europe and for the United States, for everybody, and for Greenland it's going to be incredible."

Meanwhile, Frederiksen described the signing of the deal as a "milestone in our long-standing co-operation".

"Seventy-five years ago we entered into an agreement about the defence of Greenland. Today, we're signing an even bigger and better agreement - a deal that can last forever."

The Danish prime minister stressed that the agreement "respects sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as Greenland's right to self-determination".

Jens-Frederik Nielsen said that "for Greenland, it is not only an agreement about us, it is [an] agreement with us.

"It takes into account the people of Greenland, our rights, our livelihoods and the development of our country.

"Greenland matters for North American security and for transatlantic security," he said, adding that the Nato had a key role to play in the North Atlantic in a changing security situation.

The agreement also confirmed Greenland would remain in Nato if it were to gain independence from Denmark.

The 1951 agreement already allowed the US to send as many troops as it wanted to Greenland. Washington already has more than 100 military personnel permanently stationed at its Pituffik base.

Trump had tried for months to purchase or annex Greenland, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.

He argued the Arctic island was an essential piece of his plan to build a futuristic "Golden Dome" defence system to protect the US against missile attacks.

However the deal only mentions the project once, and contains no concrete proposal.

A Nato spokesperson said shortly afterwards that the military alliance welcomed the deal, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".

In Denmark, the deal is being hailed as a triumph of diplomacy, and several political parties in Denmark have already said they would back it.

For Greenland, a country of 56,000 people, there was good reason for a big sigh of relief. Its leader sat side-by-side with the world's most powerful man, and got a deal that should now bring an end to months of crisis.

items.title: Microsoft killed FoxPro in 2007. Anyway, here's FoxPro revived
items.summary: Visual FoxPro stopped at version 9 in 2007. A surprising amount of it is still running, in 32 bits, because rewriting a 20-year-old business app is how you lose the business. A customer wanted to keep milking their app for the foreseeable future, so here it is: the same language on a new runtime (Rust, compiled to wasm, checked against the real vfp9.exe), tables no longer stopped at 2 GB, the old 32-bit .fll add-ins still loading, and lambdas, JSON and an HTTP server bolted on for good measure. Reports are not done and the builds are unsigned. MIT because why not? Comments URL: https://news.yc
items.content:
FoxDev Studio opens the projects, forms and tables you already have and runs them the way you remember: no rewrite, no conversion, no export step .

Point it at a folder you have not opened in years, and what is there is what you get.

Projects, forms, class libraries, menus and reports open straight from the files you already have. Nothing is migrated first, and nothing is left behind.

Forms, classes, menus and reports are edited where you expect them to be, alongside the project manager, the Command Window and a debugger that stops on your line.

Tables, indexes, memos and databases are read and written in place. What sits on disk afterwards is the same kind of file it was before.

The system calls, the automation objects and the old add-in libraries your application leans on keep working, so the parts nobody wants to touch stay untouched.

The IDE, on Visual FoxPro's own sample projects. Every picture is a real session.

Small differences are what break an old application: a number printed a column too wide, an event arriving a moment late, an error with the wrong number on it. So behaviour here is settled by asking Visual FoxPro itself and matching its answer, rather than by reading a reference page and hoping.

What comes out of that is a runtime written from scratch: quick to start, self-contained, and straightforward about the corners it has not reached yet.

Visual FoxPro stopped at version 9, and at 32 bits. This is the same language, rebuilt on a foundation that has not been frozen since 2007. Four pieces are what make that possible.

Visual FoxPro is a 32-bit program, and that decides more than it appears to. It is why a table stops at two gigabytes, why a memo file stops at two gigabytes, and why a big report runs out of memory on a machine with plenty to spare. The limits are signed 32-bit numbers buried in the file handling, not a licensing decision anybody made.

FoxDev Studio is 64-bit throughout . Every file offset is 64-bit and a table is never read into memory at all, so the same .dbf that used to stop dead carries on into the hundreds of gigabytes . One thing to know before you lean on it: a table grown past two gigabytes will not open in Visual FoxPro again. If you still work in both, that is a one-way door.

Visual FoxPro compiled your program to p-code and shipped a runtime to execute it. This is the same arrangement, made again: a compiler and a bytecode interpreter written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly , so one machine runs your code wherever the application runs. The editor checks what you type through that very compiler, so what it underlines and what the runtime refuses cannot drift apart.

A running program is a fiber. When it needs something from the world outside (a message box, a modal form, the next record) it does not call out and block; it yields, the work is done while the machine is off the stack, and the answer is handed back. That is why MESSAGEBOX() stops your program without freezing the window behind it, why READ EVENTS waits without spinning, and why SetFocus can fire GotFocus , and Init can run while a form is still being built, in the order FoxPro always did it.

A running form is a live tree of objects with the properties you would expect, and the interface is drawn straight from that tree by React. Each object watches only itself, so THISFORM.lblGreeting.Caption = cMsg repaints one label rather than the whole form. On a dense screen that is the difference between instant and sluggish.

The same tree is what the designer edits, one step earlier. There is no second model kept in step with the first, which is the usual place a form and its designer start telling different stories.

An .fll is a 32-bit image, and every process in a 64-bit application is 64-bit, so nothing inside the application itself could ever open one. Rather than tell you it is impossible, SET LIBRARY TO starts a small 32-bit process whose only job is to hold your library , and the runtime talks to it. The calls are synchronous, because a program may call into a library halfway through an expression, and an answer that arrived later would not be an answer. It is measured against real libraries: the encryption library, FoxTools, and libraries built from Microsoft's own API samples.

Nothing 64-bit needs the bridge: DECLARE ... DLL reaches a modern library in the same process, and automation objects are reached the way they always were. The old road stays open; it just is not the only one any more.

Everything you have written still means what it always meant. FoxScript only adds on top: a block you can hand to something else to run later, and a way to answer a web request from the code that already knows your business.

Every line of that runs on the same runtime your forms do. The queries, the cursor and the library call are ordinary FoxPro; the lambda and the server are what FoxScript adds: no second language, no service to stand up beside it. The keywords and the HTTP API are each written down in full.

The nightly is rebuilt from every push to main and published as a pre-release on GitHub. Unsigned, so the first launch asks you to confirm.

Each part of the product is written down, including the parts that are not there yet.

Work already mapped out, roughly in the order it is being built.

items.title: How Ceuta, football and Israel are shaping Morocco's election
items.summary: Young voters are being courted with football slogans, promises of jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls.
items.content:
Disillusioned young voters in Morocco were courted with viral football slogans, promises of one million jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls ahead of Wednesday's parliamentary elections.

Yet, for many young Moroccans, politics remains deeply disconnected from reality.

"I have no hope for this election. I'm ashamed of our political scene. It's a complete circus," Siham Azeroual, 32, an environmental activist who lives in the Atlas region, tells the BBC.

The outcome of the vote will decide the make-up of the next government, just weeks after 60,000 people risked their lives to cross from the North African country to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta - a sign of the lack of opportunities many young people feel they have at home.

Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy where political parties compete for 395 seats in the House of Representatives, the legislative chamber.

Yet executive power remains closely tied to the crown. King Mohammed VI, the 63-year-old monarch, appoints the prime minister from the political party that comes first in the election, but also presides over the Council of Ministers - the country's most important policy-making body.

The current campaign also follows a wave of Gen Z protests that erupted in September 2025 over unemployment, healthcare and living costs.

Demonstrators chanted slogans like "freedom, dignity, and social justice" which escalated to "get out Akhannouch", a reference to current Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch.

More than 2,400 people faced prosecution following the unrest. Despite the crackdown, some young activists are choosing to enter the political arena.

Hamza El Kharroubi, 29, was briefly arrested during the protests. He is now running for parliament with the little-known Environment and Sustainable Development Party, which has a green agenda.

"As a young person, I don't have much hope. I joined this party because they wanted more Gen Z faces and they are allowing us to speak freely about our demands," El Kharroubi tells the BBC.

He comes from Tetouan, just 34km (21 miles) from Fnideq beach, where the migration wave to Ceuta started in late July.

Some 60,000 people crossed, both Moroccans and other nationalities. At least 100 people died in the largest migration surge to the enclave in recent history.

"We want justice for the families of those who died crossing to Ceuta. We want compensation for their families," El Kharroubi says.

He argues that the crossing was widely linked to economic hardship and unemployment.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates overall unemployment stood at 13% last year, while youth unemployment - between the ages of 15 and 24 - reached 37.3%.

El Kharroubi says his goal is not to compete with established heavyweights - but securing a voice in parliament to build toward 2031.

"As young people, we have to enter the parliament so by 2031 we have strong young politicians who can compete for a seat in the government."

Fouzi Lekjaa, head of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation and a senior politician who works in the finance ministry, has emerged as the kingdom's newest political sensation - and a definite heavyweight.

Credited with helping the Atlas Lions - as the national men's football team is known - become global contenders, Lekjaa joined the centrist Party of Authenticity and Modernity (Pam) in July.

Videos of his campaign rallies have gone viral in the football-mad nation that is jointly hosting the next World Cup along with Spain and Portugal.

The clips show crowds chanting "Sir" which means "Go" in Moroccan Arabic - the iconic catchphrase from Morocco's historic 2022 World Cup run, when it became the first Arab and African side to make it to the semi-finals.

Lekjaa has promised to make Morocco sixth in the world in education and healthcare, to match the Fifa ranking of the men's football team.

Pam is competing against 26 other parties, including Prime Minister Akhannouch's National Rally of Independents (RNI). In its bid for a second term, RNI has renewed a pledge to create one million job opportunities by 2031.

Political expert Rachid Aourraz, from the Moroccan Institute for Policy Analysis (MIPA), remains sceptical about this promise.

"The slogan 'one million jobs' has become an overused electoral slogan. There is also talk of raising the minimum wage, but what is proposed cannot withstand a structural inability to create stable net jobs," Aourraz tells the BBC.

He adds that major parties "do not compete over an alternative model", but rather over how to implement public policies set by a royal vision.

Also seeking a political comeback is the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD) - using anti-Israeli sentiments to woo voters.

Morocco normalised ties with Israel in December 2020 along with several other Arab countries, under the US-brokered Abraham Accords.

Led by populist former Prime Minister Abdelilah Benkirane, the PJD is campaigning heavily on a promise to end diplomatic ties with Israel. He says the normalisation was a "mistake" made by his party which led the government between 2016 and 2021.

Bilateral ties were hit during the Gaza war with weekly protests taking place in the capital, Rabat, against the Israeli diplomatic presence.

During the conflict the Israeli liaison office was closed and direct flights between the two countries were suspended.

Yet despite an outpouring of pro-Palestinian protests, with tens of thousands taking to the streets and setting ablaze the Israeli flag at the height of the war, it was announced earlier this month that Israel and Morocco had agreed to open full embassies in their respective countries.

This followed a meeting between their top diplomats and the US ambassador to the United Nations.

"We have to speak up," Benkirane told supporters at a campaign rally in Marrakesh.

"If we work hard, the king will close the Israeli embassy. The king does not like going against his own people," he added, warning of "the dangers of Israel and Zionism in Morocco".

More than half of Morocco's total population of roughly 38.8 million is under the age of 35 - though only 4% of the more than 15.8 million registered voters are aged between 18 and 24.

"I am not keeping up much with the campaigns - but I noticed the same faces as usual," says Hiba, a 27-year-old Moroccan living in Canada who preferred not to use her last name.

She lives in Montreal which has a large Moroccan diaspora of about 104,000 people, according to the 2016 census.

Many of last year's Gen Z protests were more vocal outside the country, where young Moroccans were able to express their anger without fear of repercussions.

Hiba, who co-organised several Gen Z protests in Montreal, says she would have considered voting had she been able to find a proxy in Morocco - which is how those in the diaspora can cast their ballot.

"Gen Z protests didn't go in vain. We achieved something. At least now we see more debates with young people on state TV," she says.

But having lived through both the 20 February movement in 2011 that changed the constitution and the recent Gen Z movement, she believes change must come from a multi-faceted approach.

"I think young people should focus on the microscale - rather than running for office, helping build communities and connecting with people and then building up to the top," she says.

Despite not being fully convinced by any political campaign, she says she will be heading to her local polling station to cast her ballot.

items.title: L’Arabia Saudita ha riaperto l’oleodotto Est-Ovest, con una portata ridotta
items.content:
L’Arabia Saudita ha riaperto l’oleodotto Est-Ovest, chiuso dall’11 settembre dopo un attacco con droni che ne aveva danneggiato le strutture : la riapertura è stata confermata all’agenzia Reuters da alcune fonti, che hanno detto che una prima petroliera è stata rifornita già martedì sera. L’oleodotto Est-Ovest è lungo circa 1.200 chilometri e attraversa la penisola arabica in territorio saudita da est a ovest, dalla regione dei pozzi petroliferi di Abqaiq al porto sul mar Rosso di Yanbu. Dall’inizio della guerra in Medio Oriente, con la chiusura dello stretto di Hormuz, è diventato fondamentale per spostare il petrolio saudita verso il mar Rosso e da lì esportarlo verso l’Europa e soprattutto l’Asia.

Una decina di giorni fa un attacco attribuito a milizie filoiraniane dell’Iraq lo aveva danneggiato: la portata attuale, dopo la riapertura, è ridotta, ma non è chiaro quanto sia lontana da quella massima di 7 milioni di barili al giorno. Per recuperare una piena funzionalità serviranno ancora circa 6 settimane. Dopo la notizia della riapertura martedì il prezzo del petrolio è sceso a 97 dollari al barile, la quotazione più bassa dall’8 settembre.

items.title: Cosa c’è nell’accordo fra Stati Uniti e Danimarca sulla Groenlandia
items.summary: Non ha una data di scadenza, prevede due nuove basi militari e libertà di movimento sull'isola per le forze armate statunitensi
items.content:
Stati Uniti, Danimarca e Groenlandia hanno firmato martedì l’accordo che permetterà una maggiore presenza militare statunitense in Groenlandia. L’accordo era stato annunciato alcuni giorni fa da Donald Trump, ma in termini piuttosto vaghi: dopo la cerimonia della firma con la prima ministra danese Mette Frederiksen e con quello groenlandese Jens-Frederik Nielsen i tre governi ne hanno pubblicato il testo . Prevede che gli Stati Uniti «rinnovino ed espandano» l’attuale base militare di Pituffik e ne costruiscano altre due, a Narsarsuaq, nel sud dell’isola, e a Mestersvig, sulla costa orientale. Garantisce anche libertà di movimento alle forze armate statunitensi ed esclude la presenza di paesi che non facciano parte della NATO sull’isola.

Con la consueta retorica, Trump lo ha definito un «accordo fantastico» e «per sempre». Ma al di là delle dichiarazioni, questa firma potrebbe mettere fine alle grandi tensioni diplomatiche intorno alla Groenlandia, innescate proprio dalla dichiarata volontà di Trump di prenderne il controllo. Insisteva sin dal 2019, in modo aggressivo, per aumentare l’influenza degli Stati Uniti sulla Groenlandia, ed è arrivato a minacciare di invadere l’isola per annetterla, citando ragioni di sicurezza nazionale. Il nuovo accordo mantiene la totale sovranità del territorio groenlandese, che fa parte del Regno di Danimarca, ma ha un proprio governo dal 1979 e dal 2009 ha ampie autonomie.

Un soldato danese a Nuuk, in Groenlandia, il 16 gennaio 2026 (AP Photo/Evgeniy Maloletka)

Rispetto all’accordo già in vigore fra i due paesi , firmato nel 1951, quello attuale ha comunque alcune differenze rilevanti. Quello passato prevedeva già la possibilità di aumentare il numero di basi militari e concedeva libertà di movimento alle forze armate, questo definisce immediatamente due nuovi stanziamenti ed esplicita la possibilità di una mobilità totale, sulla terra, nello spazio aereo, nelle acque territoriali e anche negli «accessi sottomarini». Non ha una data di scadenza e prevede espressamente che l’accordo resti valido anche se la Groenlandia dovesse diventare indipendente: in quel caso si impegna a entrare nella NATO e a rilevare «diritti e doveri» della Danimarca stabiliti nell’accordo.

Il testo prevede anche che i paesi che non fanno parte della NATO non possano avere strutture militari sull’isola, anche temporanee, e che non possano avere accesso a risorse strategiche dell’isola e che potenzialmente possano «essere un pericolo per la sicurezza». La norma di fatto stabilisce che investimenti stranieri di paesi non NATO debbano essere «concordati» con l’amministrazione statunitense. La formula utilizzata è abbastanza vaga da salvaguardare la sovranità groenlandese, ma l’amministrazione statunitense la interpreta come una sorta di garanzia che paesi come Russia e Cina non possano accedere alle ingenti riserve del paese di metalli rari , necessari per la fabbricazione di microchip e altri componenti tecnologici.

L’accordo dovrà essere ratificato dal parlamento danese, dove comunque sembra godere di un diffuso sostegno: da oltre un anno la situazione della Groenlandia aveva preoccupato non poco il governo danese, che era arrivato a considerare gli Stati Uniti una possibile minaccia per la sicurezza nazionale.

Negli scorsi mesi le trattative fra Stati Uniti, Danimarca e Groenlandia erano però proseguite. La Groenlandia in passato ha ospitato molte più basi militari statunitensi di quelle previste dall’accordo: durante la Guerra fredda, gli anni di contrapposizione con l’Unione Sovietica, gli Stati Uniti ebbero fino a 17 strutture militari e 10mila soldati sull’isola.

items.title: Ukraine anger as EU removes Russian oligarchs from sanctions list
items.summary: Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman both have close ties to President Putin, and Kyiv said the move sent Moscow the wrong signals.
items.content:
The European Union is to remove sanctions on two oligarchs imposed after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, according to reports, prompting anger in Ukraine.

France had campaigned for Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov to be taken off the list, citing "national security concerns". Luxembourg called for the removal of Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman, who is suing the country for the release of frozen assets.

Latvia initially opposed the deal but agreed to a compromise, part of which involved extending sanctions on nearly 3,000 other individuals and entities for three years.

Ukrainian officials said the move was "unacceptable" and sent the wrong signal to Moscow.

"Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted: a sense of impunity, the humiliation of the EU, and division among Europeans," Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said on X.

He urged all EU member states to instead announce national sanctions on the two individuals. Latvia has already said it would do so.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov earlier welcomed the prospect of the two oligarchs being taken off the list, claiming the EU's sanctions were illegal and all Russians should be removed.

Usmanov founded USM Holding company , an investment group that owns iron, steel and copper suppliers, and the Megafon telecommunications company. He has in the past had ties with the English Premier League clubs Arsenal and Everton.

The EU froze his assets in 2022, describing him as "a pro-Kremlin oligarch with particularly close ties to Russian president Vladimir Putin". Usmanov said the decision was "unfair".

It has been reported that France's initiative was linked to a prospective prisoner release deal with Azerbaijan.

Fridman, a Russian-Israeli citizen born in Ukraine, is the founder of the Alfa Group investment conglomerate, with key interests in energy and banking. The EU has described him as a top Russian financier and enabler of Putin's inner circle.

Fridman himself said at the time of Russia's full-scale invasion that the conflict should end as soon as possible , but avoided outright condemnation of President Putin.

His Russian-Latvian business partner Pyotr Aven was stripped of Latvia's highest civilian honour in 2022 for failing to condemn the invasion of Ukraine.

This may have influenced Latvia's opposition to the move, vetoing it in a vote by EU ambassadors on Monday.

However, on Tuesday it changed its vote to an abstention as a compromise was reached. The new deal involved extending sanctions on some remaining 2,600 individuals and entities to three years. Until now, sanctions had to be renewed every six months.

Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs also announced that France had agreed to start talks with Latvia about joining a French nuclear deterrence initiative and strengthen its military presence in Latvia.
